20 mins daily of HIIT on the rowing machine can be a game changer : 1.	Burn calories in a fun fast way.   In 20 minutes, you can get a high-output session that hits hard without needing a long workout — working at 80-95% of your Max Effort it scales for wherever you are at. 2.	Build full-body fitness.   Rowing works your legs, glutes, core, back, and arms all at once, so you’re training more than just cardio. 3.	Boost heart and lung power.   HIIT pushes your aerobic engine, helping you get fitter, recover faster and feel less gassed in hard fast efforts. 4.	Improve endurance and work capacity.   The repeated intervals teach your body to handle intensity better.  Over time consistency builds and you can play with the variables of recovery.  The benefits carries over to other sport, training and everyday energy. 5.	Time-efficient and low-impact.   You get a brutal session in a short window and the rower is easier on the joints which has been a an absolute game changer. P.S so many wonderful messages about people starting to use the rowing machine more! I’ll be dropping some core workouts that I incorporate that have helped me develop an elite level of endurance and cardio and keep myself in shape. This rowing machine and mentality of rowing training can really make something out of you if you commit! #rowing #hiit #dailyworkout #routine #fitness

Braised Chicken Legs with Rice, Potatoes & Veggies🍗 Ingredients * 1 package chicken drumsticks (6–7 pieces) * 1-2 tbsp olive oil * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp black pepper * 2 tsp garlic powder * 2 tsp onion powder * 2 tsp paprika * ½ tsp cumin * 1 jalapeño, diced * ½ red onion, diced * 1 tbsp sun-dried tomato paste * 1 tbsp @Loisa sofrito * 5–6 garlic cloves, minced * 4 cups chicken stock * 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce * Small potatoes, halved (about 10–12 baby potatoes) * 1 zucchini, diced * Cooked white rice, for serving (let me know if you guys want my rice recipe) Instructions: 1. Clean the chicken with vinegar, then pat completely dry with paper towels. 2. Season the chicken with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and cumin. Toss until evenly coated. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. 4. Brown the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. It doesn’t need to be cooked through. Remove and set aside. 5. In the same pot, add the diced jalapeño and red onion. Cook for about 5 minutes until softened. 6. Stir in the sun-dried tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds. 7. Add the Loisa Sofrito and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. 8. Pour in the chicken stock and tomato sauce, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle boil. 9. Return the chicken to the pot. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the chicken is fall-apart tender and the sauce has reduced. 10. About 20 minutes before the chicken is done, add the halved potatoes and diced zucchini. Continue simmering until the potatoes are fork-tender and the zucchini is cooked. 11. Serve over fluffy white rice and spoon plenty of the sauce over the top. #chickenlegs #braised #onepotmeals #cookwithme

EASY MEALS FOR 2 EP 22 Crispy Gochujang Chicken Thighs Ingredients Really a meal for 1 because someone ate all of it :)  Chicken * 400–450 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces * 1/2 teaspoon salt * 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder * 1/2 teaspoon black pepper * 3 tablespoons cornstarch * 3–4 tablespoons neutral oil, for shallow-frying, enough to cover bottom of pan  Spicy gochujang sauce * 1 tbsp butter  * 1½ tablespoons gochujang * 1 tablespoon soy sauce * 1 tablespoon brown sugar * 1 tablespoon rice vinegar * 2 teaspoons sesame oil * 3 cloves garlic, finely minced * 1 teaspoon grated ginger * 1/4 cup water For serving * Steamed rice * Sliced green onion * Toasted sesame seeds * Cucumber, optional Instructions 1. Pat the chicken thighs dry and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt, garlic powder, black pepper. 2. Add the cornstarch and toss until the chicken is evenly coated with a thin, dry layer. 3. Heat the neutral oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and shallow-fry for 4–5 minutes per side, or until golden, crispy and cooked through. Work in batches if necessary. 4. Transfer the chicken to a plate. Carefully remove the oil, add butter to skillet. 5. Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for about 30 seconds. 6. Stir in the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, water and optional gochugaru. Simmer for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until glossy and slightly thickened. 7. Return the chicken to the skillet and toss for 30–60 seconds, until evenly coated. Don’t cook it in the sauce for too long or the coating will soften. 8. Serve immediately over rice and finish with green onion and sesame seeds. #chicken #koreanchicken #cooking #EasyRecipe #creatorsearchinsights

This routine is for anyone who is not dealing with extreme damage but wants over all glossier & softer hair this is the the exact routine I built for getting glass hair on fine hair but will work for the wavy curly hair girls too!!  the science: the flatten your cuticle lies, the more light it reflects that's what gives the illusion of glass. glossy hair isn't a product, it's the consistency of routine over time that’s keeping that cuticle smooth from prewash to final styling  it took me a while to figure out the system, but once I did, the results compounded and now I wanna share my favourite tips with you because this is the routine that actually for every  wash day. the 5 things I never skip: 1. always create a barrier before shampoo: hair oil or conditioner first. less friction = less cuticle damage = more shine 2. weekly hair mask. deep hydration is what keeps that cuticle flat and the shine consistent. 3. a glossing treatment every 3-4 weeks  this is the step that takes glossy to glass  4. leave-in conditioner every single wash. beats frizz and keeps the cuticle flat between washes. 5. the hair sandwich method oil before heat styling AND after. then always finish with a cool shot to lock the cuticle in place ✨ Hope these haircare tips help you guys!! #hair #haircare #glasshair #hairgloss

Raising Cane’s-Style Chicken Fingers With Cane’s Sauce. Ingredients: For the Chicken: - 2 lb chicken breast, cut into strips - Oil for frying For the Wet Batter: - 2 cups buttermilk - 2 tbsp garlic powder - 1 tbsp black pepper - Salt to taste - 1 tbsp smoked paprika For the Dry Batter: - 2 cups all-purpose flour - 3 tbsp cornstarch - Salt to taste - 1 tbsp garlic powder - 1 tsp black pepper - 1 tsp smoked paprika For the Cane’s Sauce: - 1 cup mayonnaise - 4 tbsp ketchup - 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce - 1 tbsp garlic powder - 1 tsp black pepper - Salt to taste - 1 tsp smoked paprika Instructions: 1. Prepare the wet batter by whisking together buttermilk, garlic powder, black pepper, salt, and smoked paprika. Add the chicken strips to the wet batter and marinate for at least 2 hours or overnight. 2. Prepare the dry batter by whisking together flour, cornstarch, salt, garlic powder, black pepper, and smoked paprika. 3. Remove the chicken from the wet batter, allowing excess to drip off, then coat each strip in the dry batter. 4. Deep-fry the coated chicken strips in hot oil (about 350°F) until golden brown and cooked through, approximately 8-10 minutes, flipping halfway through. 5. Prepare the Cane’s Sauce by whisking together mayonnaise, ketchup,Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, black pepper, salt, and smoked paprika. 6. Serve the crispy chicken fingers with Cane’s Sauce. #canessauce #raisingcanes #friedchicken #chickentenders #Recipe
